about: The games played for vibration with a DualSense or DualSense Edge on a Mac. A game is added after a session, from what was felt and what the Wine modules logged, never from what it should do. Each connection has its own result. docs/vibration.md is made from this file by tools/vibration-md.py.
stack: MacGameFix's Wine modules in a NotProton runner (CrossOver Preview 27), Steam Input off for the game, unless a result says otherwise.

results.not-recorded: Played; how it felt was not recorded
results.connection-not-recorded: Played; which connection was not recorded

games.name: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID. It plays its haptics as audio on the pad's audio output, which it finds by the audio endpoint's container.
games.description: Insomniac's PC port drives the pad itself, as on a PS5: haptics on the actuators and adaptive triggers, on a cable and over Bluetooth.

bluetooth.notes: The same as on a cable.

games.settings: Suggested: full motor power on the Edge and the Edge's haptics at 2x, on a cable and over Bluetooth.
details: It claims the motor power at 0x00 in every report for a standard DualSense, never for an Edge, which keeps its own stored reduction. With the power at full and the haptics at 2x the Edge felt like a standard DualSense.
It sends the same haptic signal to both pads (a level meter showed the same peaks and RMS for the same moments).
It reads feature reports 0x09, 0x20 and 0x05 only.
The touchpad moved the in-game camera (2026-10-20).

games.name: F1 23
games.technology: Sony's PC library (libScePad), which finds the pad over HID and plays its haptics on the pad's audio output.
games.description: Codemasters' game uses Sony's own library for the pad: haptics and trigger effects on a cable and over Bluetooth, with the Edge shown as a standard DualSense.

cable.pads: DualSense Edge shown as a DualSense, and DualSense
cable.notes: In a CrossOver Preview bottle an Edge seen as an Edge worked too: buttons, haptics and triggers.

bluetooth.pads: DualSense Edge shown as a DualSense, and DualSense; both at once
bluetooth.notes: A standard DualSense felt jerky at 1x and steady at 2x.

games.settings: Suggested: the Edge shown as a standard DualSense, and a DualSense's haptics at 2x over Bluetooth. Steam Input off: with it on, the haptics over Bluetooth started and stopped.
details: Under NotProton, as an Edge, the game assigned no buttons ("No preset control scheme", 2026-10-15).
The level meter showed the same continuous signal leaving the modules with Steam Input on or off.

games.name: FINAL FANTASY VII REBIRTH
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID; its haptics play as audio on the pad's audio output.
games.description: Square Enix's PC port plays its haptics on the pad's actuators. Played over Bluetooth: "works very well".

bluetooth.notes: "Works very well." The modules logged the game keeping 20 ms waiting in the Bluetooth haptics output.

details: The modules saw its haptics as audio and its motor power claim.

games.name: CONTROL Resonant
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID; its haptics play as audio on the pad's audio output.
games.description: Remedy's game drives the pad itself: haptics and trigger effects, on a cable and over Bluetooth.

games.name: UNCHARTED: Legacy of Thieves Collection
games.technology: Not analysed. It plays haptics as audio and sends motor values beside them.
games.description: Its haptics came with the action over Bluetooth once the modules stopped writing copies of its motor reports.

cable.notes: The haptics output was open: the game asked for 32 ms of buffer.

bluetooth.notes: The queue held 29 ms on average and 34 at most; 94 haptics reports every 2 s, nothing dropped.

details: It sends motor values all the time beside its haptics, up to about 18 control reports a second. Over Bluetooth those copies took the room the haptics need, and the haptics restarted 54 times in two minutes, until the modules stopped writing a copy while haptics stream.

games.name: Beast of Reincarnation
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID, for the haptics and triggers; it also rumbles through XInput.
games.description: Haptics and trigger effects on a cable and over Bluetooth. Its XInput rumble with the modules' XInput option is not played yet.

cable.notes: Haptics, on an earlier build of the modules.

bluetooth.notes: Haptics and triggers, in a CrossOver Preview bottle. Its motors rumbled only with Steam Input on, before the modules had an XInput rumble.

games.name: Ghost of Tsushima
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID; its haptics play as audio on the pad's audio output.
games.description: Haptics on a cable with both pads.

cable.notes: On an earlier build of the modules.

games.name: Returnal
games.description: Haptics on a cable with both pads.

cable.notes: On an earlier build of the modules.

games.name: Mortal Shell II
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID: it drives the motors and the trigger effects itself.
games.description: Its rumble and trigger effects kept working with the modules on a cable.

cable.notes: On an earlier build of the modules.

games.name: Mortal Kombat 1
games.technology: SDL 2 (SDL2.dll 2.32.0), which drives the pad over HID: the rumble as the pad's emulation of motors.
games.description: Each rumble ends with its hit, on a cable and over Bluetooth, since the Wine modules of 2026-10-20.

cable.notes: 17 rumbles in 74 s, the motors on 6 % of the time, each ended by SDL's stop.

bluetooth.notes: 15 rumbles in 38 s with a DualSense, 34 in 73 s with an Edge, none longer than about 250 ms.

games.settings: Rumble on the haptic actuators is optional over Bluetooth.
details: SDL 2 asks an Edge (firmware 0x0217) for the old emulation at half strength and a DualSense from firmware 2.24 for the improved one at full; the modules give the Edge the improved one at twice what SDL wrote, as SDL 3 would.
SDL ends a rumble with a report that has no rumble bit; over Bluetooth the modules missed it until 2026-10-20, and the rumble went on for the whole fight.

games.name: Onimusha: Way of the Sword
games.technology: XInput only: its executable reads no DualSense, and the store does not list the DualSense for it. Game Feel gives it the pad as an XInput controller.
games.description: With the pad shown as an XInput controller, its rumble plays on the motors, or on the haptic actuators if chosen.

bluetooth.notes: 82 rumbles in 218 s, 154 ms each at the median. Rumble on the haptic actuators felt right too.

games.settings: The pad as an XInput controller (by the store's rule). Trigger effects for the game from Game Feel: R2 slope, and resist while L2 is pressed.

games.name: God of War
games.technology: Sony's PC library (libScePad), which does not know the Edge.
games.description: Shown as a standard DualSense, the Edge rumbles on the motors and gets the game's lightbar. Played before the Wine modules.
games.settings: Suggested: the Edge shown as a standard DualSense.
details: 2026-10-16, NotProton's pad bridge (PR #90): rumble on the motors and the lightbar; the game sets no trigger effects.

games.name: Nioh 3
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID. It looks for the pad's audio output through SetupAPI: it reads the pad's container (SPDRP_BASE_CONTAINERID) and searches the audio render interfaces for the same one.
games.description: The game finds the pad and sets its lights and triggers, but never vibrates: Wine registers no audio device with SetupAPI, so the game never finds the pad's output, and with a DualSense it does not fall back to the motors.
games.settings: In the game: all five vibration options on, mode Immersive.
details: A Wine trace showed it asking for the audio render interfaces about 70 times a second, and getting an empty list every time.
It writes the old rumble emulation once, with both motors at 0, and never a motor value after that.
It creates and releases XAudio2 without ever playing through it.
A fix that lists Wine's audio outputs with SetupAPI is being tested (patch 0009).
